title: Bundles of ten
_map: Bundles of ten (Y2) + The counter that rolls over (Y1). Big idea: 34 = 3 tens and 4 ones, and other ways too; after 9 ones comes a new ten.
_story: The robot dropped a bucket of 34 bricks and wants to count them fast. Snapping rods of ten is the trick (like Minecraft stacks of 64, but tens). He makes 34 different ways, then the farm counter rolls past 39 and 99.
_stepChain: counting one by one is slow → snap 10 into a rod → 34 = rods + singles → the digits mean tens and ones → 34 made other ways (break a rod) → the robot thinks 2 tens and 14 ones is a different number → 39 + 1 rolls over → 99 + 1

talk.goodAnswer: 3 tens: three rods of 10 bricks. The 4 means 4 single bricks.

talk.ask: Can you make 34 in a different way?
talk.goodAnswer: yes, like 2 tens and 14 ones, or 1 ten and 24 ones. It's still 34 bricks.
the 10 ones snap together into a new ten, so it's 4 tens and 0 ones.

handsOn: Build rods of 10 Lego bricks. Make 34 with rods and single bricks. Then break one rod and make 34 a different way. Can you make 34 with no rods at all?

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: Oh dear. I dropped my bucket of bricks! There are 34 of them, all mixed up. Counting them one at a time takes me ages. Is there a faster way?
Here's a builder's trick. Snap 10 bricks into a rod. Then another. Then another. 3 rods of 10, and 4 bricks left. The rods are called tens, and the single bricks are called ones.
Now look at the number 34. The 3 tells you how many tens: 3 rods. The 4 tells you how many ones: 4 single bricks. Each digit has its own job.
Can you make 34 in a different way? Choose how many rods to keep, then tap the hammer. The other bricks stay as ones. Find all the ways.

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: Wait. 2 tens and 14 ones. That's a different number from 34, isn't it? It looks completely different!

question.prompt: Is 2 tens and 14 ones the same as 34?
question.onRight: Yes. You saw that breaking a rod doesn't lose any bricks. 20 and 14 is still 34.

1.mistake: thinks changing how it's grouped changes the amount
1.hint: Did any bricks go away when the rod was broken? Count the ones in tens: 10 and 4.
1.say: We only broke one rod into single bricks. No bricks went anywhere. 2 tens is 20, and 14 more makes 34.

question.reveal: 2 tens and 14 ones is 34. Same bricks, grouped differently.

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: My farm counter counts my chickens. It says 39: 3 tens and 9 ones. Oh look, one more chicken has arrived!

question.prompt: What will the counter show now? Make a guess.
question.reveal: 40! 9 ones and 1 more make 10 ones, and 10 ones snap together into a new ten. So it's 4 tens and 0 ones: 40. The ones go back to zero, and the tens go up.

narration.text: Here's a challenge for later. Invent your own counter! It could count in tens like ours, or something different, like groups of 5. What happens when your counter fills up?

rule.ask: Can you say what the 3 in 34 means? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: In 34, the 3 means 3 tens, and the 4 means 4 ones. And 10 ones always snap together into a new ten.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: the counter shows 99. One more chicken arrives. What does it show?
bonus.reveal: 100! 10 ones make a new ten, and then 10 tens snap together into something new: a hundred.
